summary: This closure review finds that the authors addressed the prior required revisions: the manuscript now contains an explicit preregistration→execution deviation disclosure, a concise preregistration→execution reconciliation (with archived artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes), an unambiguous reclassification of the primary estimand as degenerate/untestable under the executed shared-generation semantics (including Abstract and Introduction), and an inline citation of the transformation_manifest when explaining the absence of a global per‑item overlap table. Deterministic reconciliation and artifact hashes are present and consistent with the reported numbers. No remaining critical reproducibility or disclosure defects were found; remaining suggestions are optional presentation improvements.
optional_revisions: Add a one‑panel visual (small figure or boxed table) showing planned_maximum_model_calls (300) vs model_calls_used (150) and indicating shared_initial_candidate semantics to make generation semantics and their effect on observable discordance immediately visible.

Include a very short verification checklist (one paragraph or two‑column table) mapping the major reported numbers (complete_pair_count, model_calls_used, n11/n10/n01/n00, contamination_summary.csv) to their archived artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes for rapid auditor verification.

Consider explicitly listing the four OpenAlex identifiers (from the preregistration) in the Disclosure Statement body or a footnote to make the preregistration target set immediately discoverable from the manuscript text.
